description: The image displays two bar charts that illustrate the relationship between ambiguity metrics and Fleiss Kappa, a measure of inter-rater agreement. The left chart plots Fleiss Kappa against the standard deviation of ambiguity (Ambiguity Std), with the x-axis showing four distinct values: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.88, 0.46, 0.03, and 0.24, respectively. The bars are colored in shades of blue, with the tallest bar at 0.0 Ambiguity Std reaching a Fleiss Kappa of 0.88, and the shortest bar at 0.82 Ambiguity Std showing a value of 0.03. The right chart plots Fleiss Kappa against the maximum ambiguity (Max Ambiguity), with the x-axis showing values 1, 2, and 3. The corresponding Fleiss Kappa values are 0.89, 0.46, and 0.23, respectively. The bars are also colored in shades of blue, with the tallest bar at Max Ambiguity 1 reaching a Fleiss Kappa of 0.89, and the shortest bar at Max Ambiguity 3 showing a value of 0.23. Both charts show a general trend of decreasing Fleiss Kappa as the ambiguity metrics increase.
